This paper presents a novel approximate neural network (ANNet) framework that enables energy-efficient inference by allowing neuron activation and weight multiplication to be approximated. We develop a range of approximate neural network designs, which can be tailored to meet specific accuracy requirements while reducing energy consumption. A key issue in this field is the lack of a clear understanding of how to transfer knowledge from known to unknown tasks.  A promising approach to address this problem is Meta-learning, which aims to optimize models for multiple tasks simultaneously. A more efficient alternative is Model Pruning, which reduces the model size while preserving key performance metrics.  In this study, we investigate the potential of pruning techniques to optimize Meta-learning models for few-shot learning, exploring the impact of different pruning methods on model performance. A notable outcome of our research is that the best Meta-learning model can be made more lightweight and efficient with the aid of pruning techniques.  The results of our study are expected to inspire researchers to explore the potential of pruning techniques for optimizing Meta-learning models for few-shot learning applications.
